message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to call out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing career and other things. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Jackson works with me, and he's always bragging about how he was a top-notch boxer with a 23-0 record, one of the best in the valley. He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he used to be in great shape before he got out of his prime and became flabby. I know for a fact that most of this is probably not true because if he was really that good, there should be some records or mentions online when I Google his name. I tried that, and nothing came up. I'm 19 years old and have been training in Muay Thai for eight years. I also wrestled in high school, so I'm pretty fit and proud of my progress in martial arts and fitness. I used to be overweight too, so I understand the struggle, but I don't need to hear Jackson's constant lies about his past. We rarely hang out outside of work because he never stops talking about himself and his supposed achievements. But last weekend, we ended up hanging out, having a few beers, and watching UFC. During the fight between Blagoy Ivanov and Taito Vasa, Jackson said, "I could KO both these bums, no challenge." That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also called him out on his boxing lies and mentioned that nothing shows up when I Google his name. I challenged him to come down to my Muay Thai gym and try, saying I'd "maul" him. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some of my coworkers about it. Most of them think I'm a asshole, but a few agreed with me. So, is it right or wrong for me to call him out like that? Let's break it down. First, I think about why I did it. I was tired of him lying and bragging all the time, especially about things that I could fact-check and see were probably not true. It was annoying and made the work environment uncomfortable for me. I wanted to stand up for myself and maybe even protect others from being misled by his lies. On the other hand, calling him out in front of others, especially in a social setting like watching UFC, might have been a bit harsh. It could have made him feel embarrassed or humiliated, which might not be the best approach. Also, telling other coworkers about it afterward could have spread negativity in the workplace. I also consider the power dynamics. I'm 19, and he's 29, so there's an age gap. Maybe he felt disrespected by a younger coworker calling him out like that. It's possible that he took it personally, which led to him walking out and others thinking I was being a jerk. Another thing to think about is the intention behind my actions. Was I trying to defend myself and others, or was I just trying to make myself feel better by putting him down? If it was the former, then maybe it's somewhat justified. If it was the latter, then it might be more about my ego than anything else. I also wonder about the consequences. Did calling him out improve the work environment, or did it make things worse? If most coworkers think I'm a asshole, that might indicate that my approach was not well-received. It's possible that they saw me as confrontational rather than standing up for what's right. Maybe a better approach would have been to talk to him privately about his behavior instead of confronting him in front of others. That way, it wouldn't have been as embarrassing for him, and it might have led to a more constructive conversation. In summary, while I understand the frustration of dealing with someone who constantly lies and brags, the way I chose to address it might have been more harmful than helpful. It's important to consider the approach and setting when addressing such issues to maintain a positive and respectful work environment.
